title: Derived direct image restricted to an open
statement:
Let $f:T\to S$ be a scheme morphism and
$a:U\hookrightarrow S$ an
open immersion. In the
cartesian square
put $V=T\times_SU$, $b:V\hookrightarrow T$, and $f_U:V\to U$.
For a finite ring $\Lambda$ and
$L\in\hyperref[def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]{D^+(T_{\Et},\Lambda)}$,
restriction gives a natural isomorphism

$$
a^{-1}Rf_*L \xrightarrow{\sim} Rf_{U,*}b^{-1}L,
$$

using the
derived direct image and
inverse image functors.

proof.text: For an etale W→U, the inverse-image description [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] identifies (a^{-1}f_*F)(W) with (f_*F)(W→S), and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] evaluates this as F(T×_S W). Since V=T×_S U, this is F(V×_U W)=(f_{U,*}b^{-1}F)(W), naturally in W and F.

source.place: 03S2 (restriction to an open / direct image on the localized etale site)

proof.text: Identify V_Et with the localized slice T_Et/U via [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open]. The restriction b^{-1} is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], while [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] gives an exact extension-by-zero left adjoint b_! to this restriction. For an injective I on T_Et, Hom_{V_Et}(-,b^{-1}I)≅Hom_{T_Et}(b_!(-),I) is therefore exact contravariantly: b_! preserves short exact sequences and Hom(-,I) is exact. Thus b^{-1}I is injective.

source.place: 03S2 and 03F3 (localized site, exact restriction and extension by zero)

proof.text: Choose a bounded-below injective resolution L→I^• using [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By exactness of b^{-1} and Step 2, b^{-1}I^• is an injective resolution of b^{-1}L. Applying the Step 1 sectionwise equality degree by degree identifies a^{-1}f_*I^• with f_{U,*}b^{-1}I^•. The exactness of the module inverse images a^{-1} and b^{-1} from [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] means these complexes compute a^{-1}Rf_*L and Rf_{U,*}b^{-1}L, yielding the claimed natural isomorphism; sectionwise construction gives compatibility with further restrictions and compositions.
